objective: Maximize honest pregame win-probability quality using point-in-time information while preserving calibration, auditability, efficiency, and rollback safety.

research_clocks.horizon_selection_rule: No horizon is preferred based on 2026 outcomes until the preregistered prospective evidence gate is satisfied. Compare candidates only on genuinely captured point-in-time snapshots from the same games.

primary_hypothesis: A late multi-book market prior captured after official inactive information, optionally corrected by strictly point-in-time player/lineup information, can improve final pregame probability quality relative to the frozen T-120 incumbent without materially degrading same-horizon market calibration.
design_principles: Treat the betting market as the primary prior and strongest public benchmark.
A proprietary correction receives weight only if it adds prospective information beyond the same-horizon market.
If raw late multi-book market consensus remains best on proper scoring, it is an acceptable LevLine 4 probability backbone.
Never manufacture historical T-minus snapshots from closing odds, retrospective inactive status, or post-kickoff data.
Use proper scoring rules and calibration as the primary evaluation framework; winner accuracy is secondary.
Keep every research candidate independently removable and fail closed on source, identity, or timestamp uncertainty.

candidate_families.name: same-horizon multi-book market consensus
candidate_families.probability_construction: de-vig each eligible book, then form a robust consensus such as median logit probability
candidate_families.notes: No de-vig method is promoted solely from non-NFL literature; same-horizon NFL evidence controls.

candidate_families.name: frozen F-ST structural transform with same-horizon market
candidate_families.coefficient_policy: Use registered F-ST coefficient literals unchanged for shadow scoring only. Do not refit from 2026 outcomes.
candidate_families.notes: This tests the value of the frozen transformation at later information horizons; historical closing-market evidence is not treated as a matched-horizon backtest.

candidate_families.name: market-offset player and expected-lineup correction
inputs: official inactive state available by forecast time
restrictions: no retrospective inactive status learned after the forecast horizon
no manually tuned player point adjustments from 2026 outcomes
candidate_families.notes: After T-90, availability should use contemporaneous official inactive information where available; uncertainty remains primarily in role/performance rather than binary active status.

candidate_families.name: calibration candidates
candidate_families.fit_policy: Calibration maps must be fit on chronologically prior out-of-sample predictions only. No candidate may be fit and evaluated on the same 2026 outcomes.
candidate_families.notes: Identity is always retained because calibration can worsen an already well-calibrated market.

candidate_families.name: late weather/venue ablation
candidate_families.notes: Promote into winner probability only if it adds same-horizon Brier information beyond the market; otherwise retain for margin/total/explanation.

explicit_noncore_lanes.name: dynamic latent team strength
explicit_noncore_lanes.reason: existing LevLine candidate did not improve the registered OOS gate; no presumption of core inclusion

explicit_noncore_lanes.name: joint score distribution
explicit_noncore_lanes.reason: existing coherent score-distribution candidate improved winner accuracy but worsened Brier and margin MAE; retain only as independent research

explicit_noncore_lanes.name: large deep neural network
explicit_noncore_lanes.reason: not justified by current game-level sample size or tabular evidence; reconsider only with materially richer tracking-scale data

evaluation.slice_policy: Diagnostic slices may explain performance but cannot rescue a failed aggregate primary-metric gate.

prospective_evidence_gate.horizon_comparison: Candidate horizons must be compared on the intersection of games with valid snapshots at all horizons being compared.
prospective_evidence_gate.promotion_vs_incumbent: Candidate minus frozen T-120 F-ST Brier must be negative and the 95% paired week-block bootstrap upper bound must be below 0.
prospective_evidence_gate.same_horizon_market_gate: For a model-adjusted candidate to claim incremental model value, candidate minus same-horizon raw market-consensus Brier must be negative with corroborating calibration/log-loss evidence. If no adjustment clears this gate, raw same-horizon market consensus may remain the probability backbone.
prospective_evidence_gate.stability_gate: Aggregate advantage must not reverse materially under leave-one-week-out evaluation, and no isolated week may account for the claimed advantage.

data_integrity.2026_outcome_use: evaluation_only_for_frozen_preregistered_candidates; never use completed 2026 outcomes to rescue, retune, select thresholds, add interactions, or redefine a candidate during its active evaluation

scientific_basis: Song, Boulier & Stekler (2007), International Journal of Forecasting: NFL betting line outperformed statistical systems and experts in their sample.
Strumbelj (2014), International Journal of Forecasting: de-vig method and bookmaker identity can materially affect odds-derived probability forecasts.
Glickman & Stern (1998), JASA: dynamic state-space modeling of NFL team strength is statistically coherent, but LevLine requires its own OOS evidence before reuse.
Kull, Silva Filho & Flach (2017), AISTATS: beta calibration can avoid pathologies of logistic calibration and is appropriate as an explicit candidate rather than an assumption.
Timmermann (2006) and subsequent forecast-combination literature: estimation error can make flexible optimal weights inferior to simple or shrunken combinations.
